note: Contractor management sat outside what the December 2025 research covered. Every marker here is a design decision, carried over from the principles the research did establish: the manager works the system on behalf of the team, and a hazard that is already recorded should reach whoever is standing in the building.

markers.title: Who is in the building, before the register
markers.finding: Design decision. The research found that people report to a person rather than to a platform, and that the manager is the one who works the system on the team's behalf.
markers.decision: The module opens on the two contractors on site right now, with what they are here for and who signed them in. The register sits underneath it.
markers.rejected: Opening on the full contractor register, which is an administrative list and answers nothing a manager needs during a shift.

markers.title: The hazard briefing is recorded, not assumed
markers.finding: Design decision, built on the open hazards the system already holds for this restaurant.
markers.decision: Sign-in fills the hazard list from the restaurant's open hazards and records which ones the contractor was told about, so the card can state it afterwards.
markers.rejected: A single 'site induction given' tick, which records that something was said but never what.

markers.title: The count is the filter
markers.decision: The two records that will stop work are counted in the page sub-line and offered as one filter chip, so the manager reaches them without reading the table.
markers.rejected: A red dot on the sidebar, which says something is wrong without saying what or where.

markers.title: Show the consequence, not the data
markers.finding: Design decision, taking the lesson from the research that reports were classified after the fact and errors came back from above, which taught people the system was a way to get something wrong.
markers.decision: An expired induction marks the row, turns the status to Blocked and removes the sign-in path. The manager is never asked to work out what an expiry date means.
markers.rejected: Printing the expiry date in a column and leaving the manager to do the arithmetic on a busy shift.

markers.title: The remedy, with what it costs
markers.finding: Design decision, following the plain-language principle the research set for the reporting form.
markers.decision: The note names the fix, where it happens and how long it takes: 15 minutes at the office tablet.
markers.rejected: A tooltip, which hides the one line that decides whether the job happens today.

markers.title: Two severities, because two things are true
markers.decision: Expiring insurance is amber and does not block the visit. An expired induction is red and does. Colour carries the difference between watch this and stop.
markers.rejected: One combined compliance status, which would collapse a warning and a blocker into the same word.

markers.title: Say where the data comes from
markers.finding: Design decision, answering the research finding that the platform was configured for one workflow and handed restaurants fields they could not act on.
markers.decision: The footer says the dates are owned by the area contractor list and cannot be edited here, so nobody wastes a shift trying.
markers.rejected: An editable field that silently fails on save, or no explanation at all.
